ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a titration curve of pH changing with the volume of NaOH added; the horizontal axis is labeled Volume NaOH (mL), with tick marks including 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 mL; the vertical axis is pH. The curve shows the first relatively obvious rise at about 10 mL, and a second steeper rise at about 20 mL. Therefore, the first equivalence point can be read from the image as about 10 mL NaOH. Reasoning: According to the specified method, use the first equivalence point for the calculation. The concentration of added NaOH is 0.10 M, and the volume at the first equivalence point is about 0.010 L, so n(OH-) = 0.10 mol/L × 0.010 L = 0.0010 mol. H2C2O4 is a diprotic acid, but at the first equivalence point, every 1 mol H2C2O4 exactly consumes 1 mol OH-, so the initial amount of substance of H2C2O4 is 0.0010 mol. The volume of the original acid solution is 20 mL = 0.020 L, so concentration = 0.0010 mol / 0.020 L = 0.050 M.

What is the concentration of the $H_2C_2O_4$ solution?

A 0.10 M solution of NaOH is titrated into 20 mL of $H_2C_2O_4$, a diprotic acid, of an unknown concentration. The pH of the $H_2C_2O_4$ solution is monitored as the NaOH is added to it, resulting in the below graph.

method.method_draft: Identify the first equivalence point from the graph at approximately 10 mL NaOH. Compute moles NaOH added: 0.10 M × 0.010 L = 0.0010 mol OH-. At the first equivalence point this equals the initial moles of H2C2O4. Divide by the original acid volume, 0.020 L: 0.0010 mol / 0.020 L = 0.050 M.
